docs.title: Installation Guide
docs.text: This comprehensive guide walks you through the complete installation process for CardDemo, from prerequisites to final verification.

docs.title: Table of Contents
docs.text:
• Prerequisites
  • Installation Overview
  • Step 1: Environment Preparation
  • Step 2: Dataset Creation
  • Step 3: Source Code Upload
  • Step 4: Sample Data Upload
  • Step 5: Environment Initialization
  • Step 6: Program Compilation
  • Step 7: CICS Configuration
  • Step 8: Verification
  • Optional Module Installation
  • Troubleshooting Installation

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: Before beginning the installation, ensure you have the following:

docs.title: Mainframe Environment
docs.text:
• z/OS operating system
  • CICS Transaction Server
  • VSAM support
  • JCL execution capability
  • File transfer capability (FTP, SFTP, or similar)

docs.title: Optional Components
docs.text: For optional modules, you'll also need: - DB2: For Transaction Type Management module - IMS DB: For Credit Card Authorizations module - MQ: For Authorization and Account Extraction modules

docs.title: Access Requirements
docs.text:
• TSO/ISPF access
  • Authority to create datasets
  • Authority to define CICS resources
  • Authority to submit JCL jobs
  • File transfer access between local and mainframe

docs.title: Skills Required
docs.text:
• Basic mainframe navigation
  • Understanding of TSO/ISPF
  • Familiarity with JCL
  • Basic CICS administration knowledge

docs.title: Installation Overview
docs.text:
The installation process follows these major phases:

  1. Preparation: Clone repository and prepare environment
  2. Dataset Setup: Create mainframe datasets
  3. Code Upload: Transfer source code to mainframe
  4. Data Upload: Transfer sample data files
  5. Initialization: Execute setup JCL jobs
  6. Compilation: Compile COBOL programs
  7. CICS Setup: Configure CICS resources
  8. Verification: Test the installation

Estimated Time: 2-4 hours for base installation

docs.title: 1.1 Clone the Repository
docs.text:
Clone the CardDemo repository to your local development environment:

git clone https://github.com/aws-samples/aws-mainframe-modernization-carddemo.git
cd aws-mainframe-modernization-carddemo

docs.title: 1.2 Review the Structure
docs.text:
Familiarize yourself with the repository structure:

app/
├── asm/        # Assembler programs
├── bms/        # BMS map definitions
├── cbl/        # COBOL programs
├── cpy/        # Copybooks
├── cpy-bms/    # BMS copybooks
├── csd/        # CICS resource definitions
├── data/       # Sample data files
├── jcl/        # JCL jobs
├── maclib/     # Macro libraries
└── proc/       # JCL procedures

docs.title: 1.3 Define Your High Level Qualifier (HLQ)
docs.text:
Choose a High Level Qualifier for your datasets. This guide uses AWS.M2 as an example, but you should use your organization's naming convention.

Example HLQ: AWS.M2

docs.title: Step 2: Dataset Creation
docs.text: Create the following datasets on your mainframe system. Replace AWS.M2 with your chosen HLQ.

docs.title: 2.1 Source Code Datasets
docs.text:
Create these datasets with FB (Fixed Block) format and LRECL=80:

Dataset Name Description Format LRECL AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.JCL JCL jobs FB 80 AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.PROC JCL procedures FB 80 AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CBL COBOL programs FB 80 AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CPY Copybooks FB 80 AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.BMS BMS maps FB 80 AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.ASM Assembler programs FB 80 AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.MACLIB Macro library FB 80

docs.title: 2.2 Sample Dataset Allocation Commands
docs.text:
Using ISPF 3.2 (Dataset Utility):

ALLOCATE DATASET('AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.JCL')
  SPACE(10,5) TRACKS
  RECFM(F,B) LRECL(80) BLKSIZE(27920)
  DSORG(PO) DSNTYPE(LIBRARY)

Or using JCL:

//ALLOC    EXEC PGM=IEFBR14
//DD1      DD DSN=AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.JCL,
//            DISP=(NEW,CATLG,DELETE),
//            SPACE=(TRK,(10,5,20)),
//            DCB=(RECFM=FB,LRECL=80,BLKSIZE=27920),
//            DSNTYPE=LIBRARY

docs.title: 2.3 Data File Datasets
docs.text:
Create these datasets for sample data:

Dataset Name Description Copybook Format LRECL AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.USRSEC.PS User Security CSUSR01Y FB 80 AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.ACCTDATA.PS Account Data CVACT01Y FB 300 AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CARDDATA.PS Card Data CVACT02Y FB 150 AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CUSTDATA.PS Customer Data CVCUS01Y FB 500 AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CARDXREF.PS Card Cross Reference CVACT03Y FB 50 AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.DALYTRAN.PS.INIT Transaction Init CVTRA06Y FB 350 AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.DALYTRAN.PS Transaction Data CVTRA06Y FB 350 AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.DISCGRP.PS Disclosure Groups CVTRA02Y FB 50 AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANCATG.PS Transaction Categories CVTRA04Y FB 60 AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANTYPE.PS Transaction Types CVTRA03Y FB 60 AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TCATBALF.PS Category Balance CVTRA01Y FB 50

docs.title: 3.1 Upload Source Files
docs.text:
Transfer the source code from your local repository to the mainframe datasets:

Using FTP:

ftp mainframe.example.com
quote site recfm=fb lrecl=80 blksize=27920
cd 'AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CBL'
mput app/cbl/*.cbl
cd 'AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CPY'
mput app/cpy/*.cpy
cd 'AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.BMS'
mput app/bms/*.bms
cd 'AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.JCL'
mput app/jcl/*.jcl
cd 'AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.ASM'
mput app/asm/*.asm

Using SFTP or File Transfer Tool:

Use your organization's preferred file transfer method, ensuring: - Text mode transfer for source code - Proper EBCDIC conversion - Correct record format preservation

docs.title: 3.2 Verify Upload
docs.text:
Check that all files were transferred successfully:

TSO ISPF 3.4
Enter: AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.*

Verify member counts: - CBL: 29 members - JCL: 33 members - CPY: Multiple copybooks - BMS: Multiple map definitions

docs.title: 4.1 Upload Sample Data Files
docs.text:
Transfer sample data from app/data/EBCDIC/ to the mainframe:

Important: Use binary transfer mode to preserve data integrity.

ftp mainframe.example.com
binary
put app/data/EBCDIC/USRSEC.txt 'AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.USRSEC.PS'
put app/data/EBCDIC/ACCTDATA.txt 'AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.ACCTDATA.PS'
put app/data/EBCDIC/CARDDATA.txt 'AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CARDDATA.PS'
put app/data/EBCDIC/CUSTDATA.txt 'AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CUSTDATA.PS'
put app/data/EBCDIC/CARDXREF.txt 'AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CARDXREF.PS'
put app/data/EBCDIC/DALYTRAN.txt 'AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.DALYTRAN.PS.INIT'
put app/data/EBCDIC/DISCGRP.txt 'AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.DISCGRP.PS'
put app/data/EBCDIC/TRANCATG.txt 'AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANCATG.PS'
put app/data/EBCDIC/TRANTYPE.txt 'AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANTYPE.PS'
put app/data/EBCDIC/TCATBALF.txt 'AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TCATBALF.PS'

docs.title: 4.2 Verify Data Upload
docs.text:
Browse the datasets to verify data was uploaded correctly:

TSO ISPF 1 (Browse)
Enter: 'AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.USRSEC.PS'

Check for readable data in EBCDIC format.

docs.title: Step 5: Environment Initialization
docs.text: Execute the initialization JCL jobs in the specified sequence. Each job must complete successfully before proceeding to the next.

docs.title: 5.1 Update JCL Parameters
docs.text:
Before submitting jobs, update the HLQ in each JCL:

  1. Edit each JCL member
  2. Change all occurrences of the HLQ to match your environment
  3. Update CICS region name if different
  4. Update VSAM catalog name if required

docs.title: 5.2 Execute Initialization Jobs
docs.text:
Submit the following jobs in order:

Order Jobname Purpose Expected RC 1 DUSRSECJ Sets up user security VSAM file 0 2 CLOSEFIL Closes files opened by CICS 0 3 ACCTFILE Loads Account database 0 4 CARDFILE Loads Card database 0 5 CUSTFILE Creates customer database 0 6 XREFFILE Loads cross reference 0 7 TRANFILE Copies initial Transaction file 0 8 DISCGRP Copies Disclosure Group file 0 9 TCATBALF Copies TCATBALF file 0 10 TRANCATG Copies transaction category file 0 11 TRANTYPE Copies transaction type file 0 12 OPENFIL Makes files available to CICS 0 13 DEFGDGB Defines GDG Base 0

docs.title: 5.3 Verify Job Completion
docs.text:
For each job: 1. Check the job output for RC=0000 2. Review SYSOUT for any error messages 3. Verify VSAM files were created successfully

Check VSAM Files:

TSO ISPF 3.4
Enter: AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.*.VSAM.*

You should see: - ACCTDAT.VSAM.KSDS - CARDDAT.VSAM.KSDS - CUSTDAT.VSAM.KSDS - CARDXREF.VSAM.KSDS - TRANSACT.VSAM.KSDS - USRSEC.VSAM.KSDS - And others

docs.title: 6.1 Compilation Overview
docs.text: CardDemo programs must be compiled in the following order: 1. Assembler programs (utilities) 2. BMS maps 3. COBOL programs

docs.title: 6.2 Compile Assembler Programs
docs.text:
Submit compilation JCL for assembler programs:

Submit: AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.JCL(ASMCOMP)

Programs to compile: - MVSWAIT: Timer control utility - COBDATFT: Date format conversion utility

docs.title: 6.3 Compile BMS Maps
docs.text:
Submit BMS compilation JCL:

Submit: AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.JCL(BMSCOMP)

This compiles all BMS maps and generates symbolic copybooks.

docs.title: 6.4 Compile COBOL Programs
docs.text:
Submit COBOL compilation JCL for each program or use batch compilation:

Submit: AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.JCL(CBLCOMP)

Online Programs to Compile: - COSGN00C (Sign-on) - COMEN01C (Main Menu) - COACTVWC (Account View) - COACTUPC (Account Update) - COCRDLIC (Card List) - COCRDSLC (Card View) - COCRDUPC (Card Update) - COTRN00C (Transaction List) - COTRN01C (Transaction View) - COTRN02C (Transaction Add) - CORPT00C (Reports) - COBIL00C (Bill Payment) - COADM01C (Admin Menu) - COUSR00C-03C (User Management)

Batch Programs to Compile: - CBTRN02C (Transaction Posting) - CBACT04C (Interest Calculation) - CBSTM03A (Statement Generation) - CBTRN03C (Transaction Report)

docs.title: 6.5 Verify Compilation
docs.text:
Check that all programs compiled successfully:

TSO ISPF 3.4
Enter: AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.LOADLIB

Verify all load modules are present with recent timestamps.

docs.title: 7.1 Define CICS Resources
docs.text:
You have two options for defining CICS resources:

Option 1: Use DFHCSDUP (Recommended)

Submit the DFHCSDUP JCL with the CSD file:

Submit: AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CSD(DFHCSDUP)

This automatically defines all required resources.

Option 2: Manual Definition via CEDA

Use CEDA transaction to manually define resources. See CICS Configuration for detailed commands.

docs.title: 7.2 Define Resource Groups
docs.text:
Define the CARDDEMO resource group:

CEDA DEFINE GROUP(CARDDEMO) LIST(CARDLIST)

docs.title: 7.3 Define Programs
docs.text:
Define all COBOL programs:

CEDA DEFINE PROGRAM(COSGN00C) GROUP(CARDDEMO) LANGUAGE(COBOL)
CEDA DEFINE PROGRAM(COMEN01C) GROUP(CARDDEMO) LANGUAGE(COBOL)
... (repeat for all programs)

docs.title: 7.4 Define Transactions
docs.text:
Define all transactions:

CEDA DEFINE TRANSACTION(CC00) GROUP(CARDDEMO) PROGRAM(COSGN00C)
CEDA DEFINE TRANSACTION(CM00) GROUP(CARDDEMO) PROGRAM(COMEN01C)
... (repeat for all transactions)

docs.title: 7.5 Define Files
docs.text:
Define all VSAM files:

CEDA DEFINE FILE(ACCTDAT) GROUP(CARDDEMO) DSNAME(AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.ACCTDAT.VSAM.KSDS)
CEDA DEFINE FILE(CARDDAT) GROUP(CARDDEMO) DSNAME(AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CARDDAT.VSAM.KSDS)
... (repeat for all files)

docs.title: 7.6 Install Resources
docs.text:
Install the CARDDEMO group:

CEDA INSTALL GROUP(CARDDEMO)

Verify installation:

CEMT INQUIRE PROGRAM(COSGN00C)
CEMT INQUIRE TRANSACTION(CC00)
CEMT INQUIRE FILE(ACCTDAT)

docs.title: 8.1 Access the Application
docs.text:
1. Clear your CICS terminal
  2. Enter transaction: CC00
  3. You should see the CardDemo sign-on screen

docs.title: 8.2 Test User Login
docs.text:
Admin User: - User ID: ADMIN001 - Password: PASSWORD

Regular User: - User ID: USER0001 - Password: PASSWORD

docs.title: 8.3 Verify Core Functions
docs.text: Test each major function: 1. Sign-on (CC00) 2. Main Menu (CM00) 3. Account View (CAVW) 4. Card List (CCLI) 5. Transaction List (CT00)

docs.title: 8.4 Run Test Batch Job
docs.text:
Submit a test batch job:

Submit: AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.JCL(POSTTRAN)

Verify it completes successfully.

docs.title: Optional Module Installation
docs.text: After completing the base installation, you can install optional modules:

docs.title: DB2 Transaction Type Management
docs.text: See: Optional Module - Transaction Type Management

docs.title: IMS-DB2-MQ Credit Card Authorizations
docs.text: See: Optional Module - Credit Card Authorizations

docs.title: VSAM-MQ Account Extractions
docs.text: See: Optional Module - Account Extractions

docs.title: Common Issues
docs.text:
Issue: JCL Job Fails with S806 - Cause: Program not found in load library - Solution: Verify compilation completed successfully and load library is in STEPLIB

Issue: CICS Transaction ABEND AFCF - Cause: File not found or not open - Solution: Check file definitions and ensure OPENFIL job ran successfully

Issue: VSAM File Not Found - Cause: Dataset not cataloged or incorrect name - Solution: Verify dataset name matches CICS file definition

Issue: Compilation Errors - Cause: Missing copybooks or incorrect library concatenation - Solution: Verify SYSLIB DD statements include all copybook libraries

docs.title: Getting Help
docs.text: If you encounter issues not covered here: 1. Check the Troubleshooting page 2. Review the FAQ 3. Consult CICS and z/OS system logs 4. Raise an issue in the GitHub repository

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
After successful installation: 1. Review the User Guide to understand application features 2. Read the Admin Guide for administrative functions 3. Explore Batch Processing for batch job details 4. Consider installing Optional Modules

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This document provides complete field-level mappings between mainframe COBOL copybook structures and PostgreSQL database tables. Each mapping includes: - Source COBOL field definition - Target PostgreSQL column definition - Data type conversion rules - Validation rules - Sample data transformations

docs.title: Mapping Conventions
docs.text:
Naming Conventions: - COBOL: UPPERCASE-WITH-HYPHENS - PostgreSQL: lowercase_with_underscores

Data Type Mappings: - PIC 9(n) → BIGINT or INTEGER - PIC X(n) → VARCHAR(n) - PIC S9(n)V99 COMP-3 → DECIMAL(n+2,2) - Date strings → DATE or TIMESTAMP

docs.title: COMP-3 (Packed Decimal) Conversion
docs.text:
COBOL COMP-3 Format: - Storage: 2 digits per byte (except last byte: 1 digit + sign) - Example: PIC S9(10)V99 COMP-3 = 6 bytes - Value: 12345678.90 stored as: 12 34 56 78 90 0C (hex)

Conversion Algorithm:

public BigDecimal convertComp3ToDecimal(byte[] comp3Bytes, int scale) {
    StringBuilder digits = new StringBuilder();

    for (int i = 0; i < comp3Bytes.length; i++) {
        byte b = comp3Bytes[i];
        int highNibble = (b >> 4) & 0x0F;
        int lowNibble = b & 0x0F;

        if (i == comp3Bytes.length - 1) {
            // Last byte: digit + sign
            digits.append(highNibble);
            boolean negative = (lowNibble == 0x0D);
        } else {
            digits.append(highNibble);
            digits.append(lowNibble);
        }
    }

    BigDecimal value = new BigDecimal(digits.toString());
    return value.movePointLeft(scale);
}

docs.title: Card Number Validation (Luhn Algorithm)
docs.text:
public boolean validateCardNumber(String cardNumber) {
    int sum = 0;
    boolean alternate = false;

    for (int i = cardNumber.length() - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
        int digit = Character.getNumericValue(cardNumber.charAt(i));

        if (alternate) {
            digit *= 2;
            if (digit > 9) {
                digit = (digit % 10) + 1;
            }
        }

        sum += digit;
        alternate = !alternate;
    }

    return (sum % 10 == 0);
}

docs.title: Mainframe Timestamp Conversion
docs.text:
Mainframe Format: YYYY-MM-DD-HH.MM.SS.NNNNNN (26 characters) Example: 2025-11-21-10.30.45.123456

PostgreSQL Format: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.NNNNNN Example: 2025-11-21 10:30:45.123456

Conversion:

public Timestamp convertMainframeTimestamp(String mfTimestamp) {
    // Input: 2025-11-21-10.30.45.123456
    // Output: 2025-11-21 10:30:45.123456

    String formatted = mfTimestamp
        .substring(0, 10) + " " +  // Date part
        mfTimestamp.substring(11, 13) + ":" +  // Hour
        mfTimestamp.substring(14, 16) + ":" +  // Minute
        mfTimestamp.substring(17, 19) + "." +  // Second
        mfTimestamp.substring(20);  // Microseconds

    return Timestamp.valueOf(formatted);
}

docs.title: Password Migration Strategy
docs.text:
Important: Mainframe passwords cannot be directly migrated due to different hashing algorithms.

Options:

  1. Force Password Reset (Recommended)
  2. Set temporary password for all users
  3. Force password change on first login

  4. Send password reset email

  5. Generate Random Passwords

  6. Generate secure random password for each user
  7. Hash with BCrypt
  8. Send to users via secure channel

BCrypt Hashing:

import org.springframework.security.crypto.bcrypt.BCryptPasswordEncoder;

public String hashPassword(String plainPassword) {
    BCryptPasswordEncoder encoder = new BCryptPasswordEncoder(12);
    return encoder.encode(plainPassword);
}

docs.title: Special Conversions
docs.text:
Packed Decimal (COMP-3):

// Example: Convert PIC S9(10)V99 COMP-3 (6 bytes) to BigDecimal
public BigDecimal convertPackedDecimal(byte[] bytes) {
    long value = 0;
    boolean negative = false;

    for (int i = 0; i < bytes.length; i++) {
        byte b = bytes[i];
        int high = (b >> 4) & 0x0F;
        int low = b & 0x0F;

        if (i == bytes.length - 1) {
            value = value * 10 + high;
            negative = (low == 0x0D);
        } else {
            value = value * 100 + high * 10 + low;
        }
    }

    BigDecimal result = BigDecimal.valueOf(value).movePointLeft(2);
    return negative ? result.negate() : result;
}

Binary (COMP):

// Example: Convert PIC 9(04) COMP (2 bytes) to Integer
public int convertBinary(byte[] bytes) {
    return ByteBuffer.wrap(bytes).getShort();
}

docs.title: Customer Data Rules
docs.text:
1. Customer ID: Must be unique, 9 digits
  2. SSN: Must be unique (if provided), 9 digits
  3. Name: First and last name required, middle name optional
  4. FICO Score: Range 300-850, or 0 for not scored
  5. Date of Birth: Must be in the past, age >= 18 for primary cardholder

docs.title: Account Data Rules
docs.text:
1. Account ID: Must be unique, 11 digits
  2. Credit Limit: Must be >= 0
  3. Cash Credit Limit: Must be <= Credit Limit
  4. Current Balance: Must be >= -Credit Limit (no over-limit)
  5. Expiration Date: Must be > Open Date
  6. Active Status: Y or N only

docs.title: Card Data Rules
docs.text:
1. Card Number: Must be unique, 16 digits, pass Luhn check
  2. CVV: 3 digits
  3. Expiration Date: Must be future date
  4. Active Status: Y (Active), N (Inactive), B (Blocked), E (Expired)
  5. Card-Account Relationship: Each card must belong to exactly one account

docs.title: Transaction Data Rules
docs.text:
1. Transaction ID: Must be unique
  2. Amount: Can be positive (charge) or negative (credit/payment)
  3. Transaction Type: Must exist in transaction_types table
  4. Category Code: Must exist in transaction_categories table
  5. Card Number: Must exist in cards table
  6. Timestamp: Original timestamp <= Processed timestamp

docs.title: User Security Rules
docs.text:
1. User ID: Must be unique, 8 characters max
  2. User Type: ADMIN or USER only
  3. Password: Must be BCrypt hashed, minimum 8 characters
  4. Email: Must be unique, valid email format
  5. Status: ACTIVE, INACTIVE, or LOCKED

docs.title: Post-Migration Validation
docs.text:
-- 1. Record count validation
SELECT 'customers' as table_name, COUNT(*) as count FROM customers
UNION ALL
SELECT 'accounts', COUNT(*) FROM accounts
UNION ALL
SELECT 'cards', COUNT(*) FROM cards
UNION ALL
SELECT 'transactions', COUNT(*) FROM transactions
UNION ALL
SELECT 'users', COUNT(*) FROM users;

-- 2. Referential integrity checks
-- Accounts without customers
SELECT COUNT(*) as orphaned_accounts
FROM accounts a
LEFT JOIN customers c ON a.customer_id = c.customer_id
WHERE c.customer_id IS NULL;

-- Cards without accounts
SELECT COUNT(*) as orphaned_cards
FROM cards c
LEFT JOIN accounts a ON c.account_id = a.account_id
WHERE a.account_id IS NULL;

-- Transactions without cards
SELECT COUNT(*) as orphaned_transactions
FROM transactions t
LEFT JOIN cards c ON t.card_number = c.card_number
WHERE c.card_number IS NULL;

-- 3. Data quality checks
-- Null values in required fields
SELECT 'customers' as table_name, 
       COUNT(*) as null_first_names
FROM customers 
WHERE first_name IS NULL;

SELECT 'customers' as table_name,
       COUNT(*) as null_last_names
FROM customers
WHERE last_name IS NULL;

-- Invalid credit limits
SELECT COUNT(*) as invalid_credit_limits
FROM accounts
WHERE credit_limit < 0 OR cash_credit_limit > credit_limit;

-- Invalid card numbers (Luhn check)
-- (Requires custom function)

-- 4. Business rule validation
-- Customers under 18
SELECT COUNT(*) as underage_customers
FROM customers
WHERE date_of_birth > CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '18 years';

-- Expired cards still active
SELECT COUNT(*) as expired_active_cards
FROM cards
WHERE expiration_date < CURRENT_DATE AND active_status = 'Y';

-- Over-limit accounts
SELECT COUNT(*) as overlimit_accounts
FROM accounts
WHERE current_balance > credit_limit;

-- 5. Sample data verification
-- Random sample of 10 customers
SELECT customer_id, first_name, last_name, ssn, fico_credit_score
FROM customers
ORDER BY RANDOM()
LIMIT 10;

-- Random sample of 10 transactions
SELECT transaction_id, transaction_type, amount, card_number, 
       original_timestamp, processed_timestamp
FROM transactions
ORDER BY RANDOM()
LIMIT 10;

docs.title: CardDemo Migration Plan: Mainframe to Java Microservices
docs.text: Comprehensive migration plan for modernizing CardDemo from mainframe (COBOL/CICS/VSAM) to Java microservices with PostgreSQL database.

docs.title: Table of Contents
docs.text:
• Executive Summary
  • Current State Analysis
  • Target Architecture
  • Microservices Decomposition
  • Data Migration Strategy
  • Technology Stack
  • Implementation Roadmap
  • Risk Assessment
  • Success Criteria

docs.title: Migration Overview
docs.text:
Objective: Modernize the CardDemo credit card management application from mainframe technologies to cloud-native Java microservices architecture.

Current State: Mainframe application with 29 COBOL programs, 10 VSAM files, 14 CICS transactions, 33 batch jobs

Target State: Cloud-native microservices application with Java Spring Boot, PostgreSQL database, REST APIs, and modern UI

Migration Approach: Strangler Fig Pattern - Incremental migration with coexistence of old and new systems

Estimated Duration: 12-18 months (depending on team size and resources)

Key Benefits: - Cloud scalability and elasticity - Modern development practices (CI/CD, DevOps) - Improved maintainability and agility - Cost reduction (mainframe licensing) - Enhanced user experience - API-first architecture for integration

docs.title: Online Programs (29 COBOL Programs)
docs.text:
User Functions: - COSGN00C - Sign-on and authentication - COMEN01C - Main menu navigation - COACTVWC, COACTUPC - Account view and update - COCRDLIC, COCRDSLC, COCRDUPC - Card management - COTRN00C, COTRN01C, COTRN02C - Transaction management - COBIL00C - Bill payment processing - CORPT00C - Report generation

Admin Functions: - COADM01C - Admin menu - COUSR00C, COUSR01C, COUSR02C, COUSR03C - User management (CRUD)

Optional Modules: - COPAUA0C, COPAUS0C, COPAUS1C - Authorization processing (IMS-DB2-MQ) - COTRTLIC, COTRTUPC - Transaction type management (DB2) - CODATE01, COACCT01 - Account extraction (VSAM-MQ)

docs.title: Batch Programs (33 JCL Jobs)
docs.text:
Daily Processing: - CBTRN02C - Transaction posting - CBTRN03C - Transaction reports - Transaction backup and indexing

Monthly Processing: - CBACT04C - Interest calculation - CBSTM03A - Statement generation

Data Management: - File initialization and loading - Data extraction and transformation - Backup and recovery

docs.title: Data Stores (10 VSAM Files)
docs.text:
• ACCTDAT - Account master (300 bytes/record)
  • CARDDAT - Card master (150 bytes/record)
  • CUSTDAT - Customer master (500 bytes/record)
  • CARDXREF - Cross-reference (50 bytes/record)
  • TRANSACT - Transaction history (350 bytes/record)
  • USRSEC - User security (80 bytes/record)
  • TRANTYPE, TRANCATG, DISCGRP, TCATBALF - Reference data

docs.title: Optional Data Stores
docs.text:
• DB2 - Transaction types, fraud tracking
  • IMS DB - Authorization details (hierarchical)
  • MQ - Message queuing for async processing

docs.title: Architecture Characteristics
docs.text:
Presentation Layer: - 3270 terminal screens (BMS maps) - Character-based UI (24x80) - Function key navigation

Business Logic: - COBOL programs with embedded business rules - Pseudo-conversational CICS transactions - Copybook-based data structures

Data Access: - VSAM indexed files (KSDS) - Alternate indexes for secondary keys - Batch/online file sharing with locking

Integration: - MQ for asynchronous messaging - DB2 for relational data - IMS DB for hierarchical data

docs.title: Technical Debt Assessment
docs.text:
Challenges: 1. Monolithic Structure: Tight coupling between presentation, business logic, and data access 2. Technology Lock-in: Mainframe-specific technologies (COBOL, CICS, VSAM) 3. Limited Scalability: Vertical scaling only, expensive hardware 4. Maintenance Burden: Aging technology, limited developer pool 5. Integration Complexity: Difficult to integrate with modern systems 6. User Experience: Outdated terminal-based interface 7. Testing Challenges: Limited automated testing capabilities 8. Deployment Rigidity: Infrequent releases, complex deployment process

Strengths to Preserve: 1. Business Logic: Well-tested, proven business rules 2. Data Integrity: ACID transactions, data consistency 3. Performance: Optimized for high-volume transaction processing 4. Reliability: Proven stability and uptime 5. Security: Robust authentication and authorization

docs.title: Architecture Principles
docs.text:
1. Microservices: Decompose monolith into independently deployable services
  2. API-First: RESTful APIs for all service interactions
  3. Cloud-Native: Designed for cloud deployment (AWS, Azure, GCP)
  4. Event-Driven: Asynchronous communication where appropriate
  5. Stateless: Services maintain no session state
  6. Database per Service: Each microservice owns its data
  7. Containerized: Docker containers for consistent deployment
  8. DevOps: CI/CD pipelines, automated testing, monitoring

docs.title: Technology Architecture
docs.text:
Frontend: - React or Angular for web application - React Native or native iOS/Android for mobile - Material-UI or Bootstrap for UI components - Redux or NgRx for state management

API Gateway: - Spring Cloud Gateway or Kong - OAuth 2.0 / JWT for authentication - Rate limiting and throttling - Request routing and load balancing

Microservices: - Java 17+ with Spring Boot 3.x - Spring Cloud for microservices patterns - Spring Data JPA for data access - Spring Security for authentication/authorization - RESTful APIs with OpenAPI/Swagger documentation

Data Layer: - PostgreSQL 15+ for relational data - Redis for caching - Flyway or Liquibase for schema migration - Connection pooling (HikariCP)

Messaging: - Apache Kafka for event streaming - RabbitMQ or AWS SQS for message queuing - Spring Cloud Stream for messaging abstraction

Infrastructure: - Docker for containerization - Kubernetes for orchestration - Service mesh (Istio or Linkerd) for service communication - Prometheus + Grafana for monitoring - ELK Stack (Elasticsearch, Logstash, Kibana) for logging - Jaeger or Zipkin for distributed tracing

CI/CD: - Jenkins, GitLab CI, or GitHub Actions - SonarQube for code quality - JUnit, Mockito for unit testing - Testcontainers for integration testing - Selenium or Cypress for E2E testing

docs.title: 1. Customer Service
docs.text:
Responsibility: Manage customer information and profiles

Functionality: - Customer CRUD operations - Customer search and lookup - Customer profile management - Address and contact management

Data Owned: - Customer master data (from CUSTDAT)

APIs: - POST /api/customers - Create customer - GET /api/customers/{id} - Get customer details - PUT /api/customers/{id} - Update customer - DELETE /api/customers/{id} - Delete customer - GET /api/customers/search - Search customers

Source Programs: - Customer data access from CVCUS01Y copybook

docs.title: 2. Account Service
docs.text:
Responsibility: Manage credit card accounts

Functionality: - Account CRUD operations - Account balance management - Credit limit management - Account status management - Account-customer relationship

Data Owned: - Account master data (from ACCTDAT) - Account-customer relationships (from CARDXREF)

APIs: - POST /api/accounts - Create account - GET /api/accounts/{id} - Get account details - PUT /api/accounts/{id} - Update account - GET /api/accounts/{id}/balance - Get balance - PUT /api/accounts/{id}/credit-limit - Update credit limit - GET /api/customers/{customerId}/accounts - Get customer accounts

Source Programs: - COACTVWC - Account view logic - COACTUPC - Account update logic

docs.title: 3. Card Service
docs.text:
Responsibility: Manage credit cards

Functionality: - Card CRUD operations - Card issuance and activation - Card status management (active, blocked, expired) - Card-account relationship - Card validation (Luhn algorithm)

Data Owned: - Card master data (from CARDDAT) - Card cross-reference (from CARDXREF)

APIs: - POST /api/cards - Issue new card - GET /api/cards/{cardNumber} - Get card details - PUT /api/cards/{cardNumber} - Update card - PUT /api/cards/{cardNumber}/status - Update card status - GET /api/accounts/{accountId}/cards - Get account cards - POST /api/cards/{cardNumber}/validate - Validate card

Source Programs: - COCRDLIC - Card list logic - COCRDSLC - Card view logic - COCRDUPC - Card update logic

docs.title: 4. Transaction Service
docs.text:
Responsibility: Process and manage transactions

Functionality: - Transaction creation and posting - Transaction history and search - Transaction categorization - Transaction validation - Real-time balance updates

Data Owned: - Transaction history (from TRANSACT) - Transaction types (from TRANTYPE) - Transaction categories (from TRANCATG)

APIs: - POST /api/transactions - Create transaction - GET /api/transactions/{id} - Get transaction details - GET /api/cards/{cardNumber}/transactions - Get card transactions - GET /api/accounts/{accountId}/transactions - Get account transactions - POST /api/transactions/search - Search transactions - GET /api/transactions/types - Get transaction types

Source Programs: - COTRN00C - Transaction list logic - COTRN01C - Transaction view logic - COTRN02C - Transaction add logic - CBTRN02C - Transaction posting logic

Events Published: - TransactionCreated - TransactionPosted - TransactionFailed

docs.title: 5. Payment Service
docs.text:
Responsibility: Process bill payments

Functionality: - Payment processing - Payment validation - Balance adjustment - Payment history

Data Owned: - Payment transactions (subset of TRANSACT)

APIs: - POST /api/payments - Process payment - GET /api/payments/{id} - Get payment details - GET /api/accounts/{accountId}/payments - Get account payments - POST /api/payments/validate - Validate payment

Source Programs: - COBIL00C - Bill payment logic

Events Published: - PaymentProcessed - PaymentFailed

docs.title: 6. Report Service
docs.text:
Responsibility: Generate reports and statements

Functionality: - Transaction reports - Account statements - Summary reports - Report scheduling - Report export (PDF, CSV)

Data Owned: - Report definitions - Scheduled reports

APIs: - POST /api/reports/transactions - Generate transaction report - POST /api/reports/statements/{accountId} - Generate statement - GET /api/reports/{id} - Get report - GET /api/reports/{id}/download - Download report

Source Programs: - CORPT00C - Report generation logic - CBSTM03A - Statement generation logic

docs.title: 7. User Service
docs.text:
Responsibility: Manage application users and authentication

Functionality: - User registration and management - User authentication - Password management - User roles and permissions - Session management

Data Owned: - User credentials (from USRSEC) - User profiles - User sessions

APIs: - POST /api/users/register - Register user - POST /api/users/login - User login - POST /api/users/logout - User logout - GET /api/users/{id} - Get user details - PUT /api/users/{id} - Update user - PUT /api/users/{id}/password - Change password - DELETE /api/users/{id} - Delete user

Source Programs: - COSGN00C - Sign-on logic - COUSR00C, COUSR01C, COUSR02C, COUSR03C - User management logic

docs.title: 8. Authorization Service (Optional Module)
docs.text:
Responsibility: Real-time transaction authorization

Functionality: - Authorization request processing - Fraud detection - Authorization history - Authorization rules engine

Data Owned: - Authorization history - Fraud tracking data

APIs: - POST /api/authorizations - Process authorization - GET /api/authorizations/{id} - Get authorization details - GET /api/cards/{cardNumber}/authorizations - Get card authorizations - PUT /api/authorizations/{id}/fraud - Mark as fraud

Source Programs: - COPAUA0C - Authorization processing logic - COPAUS0C, COPAUS1C - Authorization inquiry logic

Events Consumed: - AuthorizationRequest (from MQ)

Events Published: - AuthorizationApproved - AuthorizationDeclined - FraudDetected

docs.title: Service Communication Patterns
docs.text:
Synchronous (REST): - User Service → Customer Service (get customer details) - Account Service → Customer Service (validate customer) - Card Service → Account Service (validate account) - Transaction Service → Card Service (validate card) - Transaction Service → Account Service (update balance)

Asynchronous (Events): - Transaction Service → Payment Service (transaction posted) - Transaction Service → Report Service (transaction created) - Authorization Service → Transaction Service (authorization approved) - Payment Service → Account Service (payment processed)

Data Consistency: - Saga pattern for distributed transactions - Event sourcing for audit trail - Eventual consistency where appropriate - Compensating transactions for rollback

docs.title: PostgreSQL Schema Structure
docs.text: Database per Service Pattern: - customer_db - Customer Service database - account_db - Account Service database - card_db - Card Service database - transaction_db - Transaction Service database - user_db - User Service database - payment_db - Payment Service database - report_db - Report Service database

docs.title: Customer Schema (customer_db)
docs.text:
Source: CUSTDAT VSAM file (CVCUS01Y copybook)

CREATE TABLE customers (
    customer_id BIGINT PRIMARY KEY,
    first_name VARCHAR(25) NOT NULL,
    middle_name VARCHAR(25),
    last_name VARCHAR(25) NOT NULL,
    address_line1 VARCHAR(50),
    address_line2 VARCHAR(50),
    address_line3 VARCHAR(50),
    state_code VARCHAR(2),
    country_code VARCHAR(3),
    zip_code VARCHAR(10),
    phone_number1 VARCHAR(15),
    phone_number2 VARCHAR(15),
    ssn VARCHAR(9),
    govt_issued_id VARCHAR(20),
    date_of_birth DATE,
    eft_account_id VARCHAR(10),
    primary_card_holder_ind CHAR(1),
    fico_credit_score SMALLINT,
    created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    updated_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    version INTEGER DEFAULT 0
);

CREATE INDEX idx_customers_ssn ON customers(ssn);
CREATE INDEX idx_customers_name ON customers(last_name, first_name);

Migration Notes: - CUST-ID (PIC 9(09)) → customer_id (BIGINT) - Date format conversion: YYYY-MM-DD string → DATE type - Add audit columns: created_at, updated_at, version - Add indexes for common queries

Source: ACCTDAT VSAM file (CVACT01Y copybook)

CREATE TABLE accounts (
    account_id BIGINT PRIMARY KEY,
    customer_id BIGINT NOT NULL,
    active_status CHAR(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'Y',
    current_balance DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0.00,
    credit_limit DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL,
    cash_credit_limit DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL,
    open_date DATE NOT NULL,
    expiration_date DATE NOT NULL,
    reissue_date DATE,
    current_cycle_credit DECIMAL(12,2) DEFAULT 0.00,
    current_cycle_debit DECIMAL(12,2) DEFAULT 0.00,
    address_zip VARCHAR(10),
    group_id VARCHAR(10),
    created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    updated_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    version INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    CONSTRAINT chk_balance CHECK (current_balance >= -credit_limit),
    CONSTRAINT chk_credit_limit CHECK (credit_limit >= 0),
    CONSTRAINT chk_cash_limit CHECK (cash_credit_limit <= credit_limit)
);

CREATE INDEX idx_accounts_customer ON accounts(customer_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_accounts_status ON accounts(active_status);

-- Account-Customer relationship
CREATE TABLE account_customers (
    account_id BIGINT NOT NULL,
    customer_id BIGINT NOT NULL,
    relationship_type VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL, -- PRIMARY, JOINT, AUTHORIZED
    created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    PRIMARY KEY (account_id, customer_id)
);

Migration Notes: - ACCT-ID (PIC 9(11)) → account_id (BIGINT) - COMP-3 amounts → DECIMAL(12,2) - Add foreign key to customer (from CARDXREF) - Add check constraints for business rules - Separate table for account-customer relationships

docs.title: Card Schema (card_db)
docs.text:
Source: CARDDAT VSAM file (CVACT02Y copybook)

CREATE TABLE cards (
    card_number VARCHAR(16) PRIMARY KEY,
    account_id BIGINT NOT NULL,
    cvv_code VARCHAR(3) NOT NULL,
    embossed_name VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    expiration_date DATE NOT NULL,
    active_status CHAR(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'Y',
    card_type VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'CREDIT', -- CREDIT, DEBIT
    issue_date DATE DEFAULT CURRENT_DATE,
    created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    updated_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    version INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    CONSTRAINT chk_card_status CHECK (active_status IN ('Y', 'N', 'B', 'E'))
);

CREATE INDEX idx_cards_account ON cards(account_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_cards_status ON cards(active_status);
CREATE INDEX idx_cards_expiration ON cards(expiration_date);

-- Card-Account-Customer cross reference
CREATE TABLE card_xref (
    card_number VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL,
    account_id BIGINT NOT NULL,
    customer_id BIGINT NOT NULL,
    created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    PRIMARY KEY (card_number, account_id, customer_id)
);

Migration Notes: - CARD-NUM (PIC 9(16)) → card_number (VARCHAR(16)) - Add card_type for future expansion - Add issue_date for tracking - Preserve CARDXREF structure

docs.title: Transaction Schema (transaction_db)
docs.text:
Source: TRANSACT VSAM file (CVTRA05Y copybook)

CREATE TABLE transactions (
    transaction_id VARCHAR(16) PRIMARY KEY,
    transaction_type VARCHAR(2) NOT NULL,
    category_code VARCHAR(4),
    source VARCHAR(10),
    description VARCHAR(100),
    amount DECIMAL(11,2) NOT NULL,
    card_number VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL,
    merchant_id VARCHAR(9),
    merchant_name VARCHAR(50),
    merchant_city VARCHAR(50),
    merchant_zip VARCHAR(10),
    original_timestamp TIMESTAMP NOT NULL,
    processed_timestamp TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    status VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'POSTED', -- PENDING, POSTED, REVERSED
    created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    version INTEGER DEFAULT 0
);

CREATE INDEX idx_transactions_card ON transactions(card_number, original_timestamp DESC);
CREATE INDEX idx_transactions_date ON transactions(original_timestamp);
CREATE INDEX idx_transactions_type ON transactions(transaction_type);
CREATE INDEX idx_transactions_status ON transactions(status);

-- Transaction types reference
CREATE TABLE transaction_types (
    type_code VARCHAR(2) PRIMARY KEY,
    type_name VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    description VARCHAR(100),
    debit_credit_indicator CHAR(1) NOT NULL, -- D=Debit, C=Credit
    created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

-- Transaction categories reference
CREATE TABLE transaction_categories (
    category_code VARCHAR(4) PRIMARY KEY,
    category_name VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    description VARCHAR(100),
    created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

Migration Notes: - TRAN-ID (PIC X(16)) → transaction_id (VARCHAR(16)) - COMP-3 amount → DECIMAL(11,2) - Timestamp conversion from mainframe format - Add status field for transaction lifecycle - Separate tables for reference data - Partition by date for performance (monthly partitions)

docs.title: User Schema (user_db)
docs.text:
Source: USRSEC VSAM file (CSUSR01Y copybook)

CREATE TABLE users (
    user_id VARCHAR(8) PRIMARY KEY,
    first_name VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
    last_name VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
    email VARCHAR(100) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
    password_hash VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL, -- BCrypt hash
    user_type VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL, -- ADMIN, USER
    status VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'ACTIVE', -- ACTIVE, INACTIVE, LOCKED
    last_login TIMESTAMP,
    failed_login_attempts INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    password_changed_at TIMESTAMP,
    created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    updated_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    version INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    CONSTRAINT chk_user_type CHECK (user_type IN ('ADMIN', 'USER'))
);

CREATE INDEX idx_users_email ON users(email);
CREATE INDEX idx_users_type ON users(user_type);

-- User roles and permissions
CREATE TABLE user_roles (
    user_id VARCHAR(8) NOT NULL,
    role_name VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    granted_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    PRIMARY KEY (user_id, role_name)
);

CREATE TABLE roles (
    role_name VARCHAR(50) PRIMARY KEY,
    description VARCHAR(100),
    created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

CREATE TABLE permissions (
    permission_name VARCHAR(50) PRIMARY KEY,
    description VARCHAR(100),
    created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

CREATE TABLE role_permissions (
    role_name VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    permission_name VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (role_name, permission_name)
);

Migration Notes: - SEC-USR-ID (PIC X(08)) → user_id (VARCHAR(8)) - Password migration: Re-hash with BCrypt (users must reset) - Add email field (required for modern auth) - Expand user type to role-based access control - Add security fields (failed attempts, password expiry)

docs.title: Phase 1: Schema Creation
docs.text:
1. Create PostgreSQL databases for each service
  2. Run DDL scripts to create tables, indexes, constraints

docs.title: Phase 2: Historical Data Migration
docs.text:
Approach: One-time bulk migration of historical data

Tools: - Custom Java migration utility - Spring Batch for large-volume processing - JDBC for database connectivity - CSV as intermediate format

Process: 1. Extract from VSAM files: - Use COBOL programs or file utilities to export VSAM to CSV - One CSV file per VSAM file - Include all records with proper field delimiters

  1. Transform data:
  2. Convert data types (COMP-3 to decimal, dates to ISO format)
  3. Handle null values and defaults
  4. Validate data integrity
  5. Generate surrogate keys if needed

  6. Split data across microservice databases

  7. Load into PostgreSQL:

  8. Use COPY command for bulk loading
  9. Disable indexes during load, rebuild after
  10. Load in dependency order (customers → accounts → cards → transactions)
  11. Validate record counts and data integrity

Migration Script Example:

@Component
public class VsamToPostgresMigrator {

    @Autowired
    private JdbcTemplate jdbcTemplate;

    public void migrateCustomers(String csvFilePath) {
        String sql = "COPY customers (customer_id, first_name, middle_name, " +
                    "last_name, address_line1, ...) " +
                    "FROM '" + csvFilePath + "' " +
                    "DELIMITER ',' CSV HEADER";
        jdbcTemplate.execute(sql);
    }

    public void migrateAccounts(String csvFilePath) {
        // Similar COPY command for accounts
    }

    // ... other migration methods
}

docs.title: Phase 3: Incremental Data Sync
docs.text:
Approach: Keep mainframe and PostgreSQL in sync during transition

Options:

Option A: Dual Write Pattern - Application writes to both VSAM and PostgreSQL - Read from PostgreSQL, fallback to VSAM - Requires modification of COBOL programs

Option B: Change Data Capture (CDC) - Capture changes from VSAM files - Replicate to PostgreSQL in near real-time - Tools: IBM InfoSphere CDC, custom batch jobs

Option C: Event-Based Sync - Publish events for all data changes - Event consumers update PostgreSQL - Kafka or MQ as event bus

Recommended: Option C (Event-Based Sync) - Least intrusive to mainframe - Enables gradual migration - Provides audit trail

docs.title: Phase 4: Data Validation
docs.text:
Validation Checks: 1. Record count comparison (VSAM vs PostgreSQL) 2. Sample data verification (random records) 3. Referential integrity checks 4. Business rule validation 5. Performance testing

Validation Script:

-- Count validation
SELECT 'CUSTOMERS' as table_name, COUNT(*) as pg_count FROM customers;
-- Compare with VSAM record count

-- Sample data validation
SELECT * FROM customers WHERE customer_id = 1;
-- Compare with VSAM record

-- Referential integrity
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM accounts a 
LEFT JOIN customers c ON a.customer_id = c.customer_id 
WHERE c.customer_id IS NULL;
-- Should return 0

docs.title: Data Synchronization Strategy
docs.text:
During Migration Period: 1. Mainframe remains system of record 2. PostgreSQL is read replica 3. Sync frequency: Real-time (events) or batch (hourly/daily) 4. Conflict resolution: Mainframe wins

After Cutover: 1. PostgreSQL becomes system of record 2. Mainframe decommissioned or archived 3. No more synchronization needed

Alternatives Considered: - Quarkus: Better for cloud-native, smaller footprint - Micronaut: Faster startup, lower memory - Recommendation: Spring Boot for enterprise maturity

docs.title: Migration Strategy: Strangler Fig Pattern
docs.text:
Approach: Gradually replace mainframe functionality with microservices while both systems coexist.

Benefits: - Reduced risk (incremental migration) - Continuous delivery of value - Ability to rollback if needed - Learn and adapt during migration

docs.title: Phase 0: Foundation (Months 1-2)
docs.text:
Objectives: Set up infrastructure and tooling

Activities: 1. Team Formation: - Assemble migration team (Java developers, DBAs, DevOps, architects) - Training on Spring Boot, microservices, PostgreSQL - Establish roles and responsibilities

  1. Infrastructure Setup:
  2. Set up development, staging, production environments
  3. Configure Kubernetes clusters
  4. Set up CI/CD pipelines

  5. Configure monitoring and logging

  6. Development Standards:

  7. Define coding standards and conventions
  8. Set up code templates and archetypes
  9. Configure SonarQube rules

  10. Establish Git workflow

  11. Architecture Validation:

  12. Build proof-of-concept for one microservice
  13. Validate technology choices
  14. Test integration patterns
  15. Performance baseline

Deliverables: - Infrastructure environments ready - CI/CD pipelines operational - Development standards documented - POC microservice deployed

docs.title: Phase 1: User Authentication & Authorization (Months 3-4)
docs.text:
Objectives: Migrate user management and authentication

Microservices: - User Service

Activities: 1. Database Migration: - Create user_db schema in PostgreSQL - Migrate USRSEC data to users table - Implement password re-hashing (BCrypt)

  2. Implement User Service with Spring Boot

  11. API Gateway configuration

  15. Unit tests (80%+ coverage)
  16. Integration tests
  17. Security testing
  18. Performance testing

Success Criteria: - Users can log in via new UI - Authentication handled by User Service - Session management with JWT - Performance: < 200ms response time - Zero downtime deployment

Mainframe Programs Replaced: - COSGN00C (Sign-on) - COUSR00C, COUSR01C, COUSR02C, COUSR03C (User management)

docs.title: Timeline Summary
docs.text:
Phase Duration Microservices Key Deliverables Phase 0 Months 1-2 - Infrastructure, POC Phase 1 Months 3-4 User Service Authentication & user management Phase 2 Months 5-7 Customer, Account Services Customer & account management Phase 3 Months 8-9 Card Service Card management Phase 4 Months 10-12 Transaction, Payment Services Transaction processing Phase 5 Months 13-14 Report Service Reporting & batch Phase 6 Months 15-16 Authorization, TranType Services Optional modules Phase 7 Months 17-18 - Cutover & decommissioning

Team Size Estimate: - 4-6 Backend Developers (Java/Spring Boot) - 2-3 Frontend Developers (React/Angular) - 1-2 DBAs (PostgreSQL) - 1-2 DevOps Engineers - 1 Architect - 1 QA Lead + 2-3 QA Engineers - 1 Project Manager - 1 Business Analyst

docs.title: Risk 1: Data Migration Complexity
docs.text:
Probability: High Impact: High Description: Migrating large volumes of data from VSAM to PostgreSQL with data integrity

Mitigation: - Comprehensive data validation scripts - Pilot migration with subset of data - Automated reconciliation tools - Rollback procedures - Data synchronization during transition

docs.title: Risk 2: Performance Degradation
docs.text:
Probability: Medium Impact: High Description: Microservices may not match mainframe performance

Mitigation: - Performance testing early and often - Database indexing and query optimization - Caching strategy (Redis) - Load testing with production-like volumes - Performance monitoring and tuning

docs.title: Risk 3: Distributed Transaction Complexity
docs.text:
Probability: High Impact: Medium Description: Managing data consistency across microservices

Mitigation: - Saga pattern implementation - Event sourcing for audit trail - Compensating transactions - Idempotent operations - Comprehensive testing of failure scenarios

docs.title: Risk 4: Integration Issues
docs.text:
Probability: Medium Impact: Medium Description: Service-to-service communication failures

Mitigation: - Circuit breaker pattern (Resilience4j) - Retry mechanisms with exponential backoff - Fallback strategies - Service mesh for reliability - Comprehensive integration testing

docs.title: Risk 5: Security Vulnerabilities
docs.text:
Probability: Medium Impact: High Description: Security gaps in new architecture

Mitigation: - Security testing (OWASP, penetration testing) - OAuth 2.0 + JWT for authentication - API Gateway for centralized security - Regular security audits - Compliance validation (PCI-DSS if applicable)

docs.title: Risk 6: Extended Timeline
docs.text:
Probability: Medium Impact: High Description: Migration takes longer than planned

Mitigation: - Phased approach with incremental value - Regular progress reviews - Adjust scope if needed - Parallel teams for different phases - Clear milestones and checkpoints

docs.title: Risk 7: User Adoption Issues
docs.text:
Probability: Medium Impact: Medium Description: Users resist new UI/UX

Mitigation: - User involvement in design - Training and documentation - Gradual rollout with feedback - Support team ready - Maintain familiar workflows where possible

docs.title: Risk 8: Budget Overruns
docs.text:
Probability: Medium Impact: High Description: Migration costs exceed budget

Mitigation: - Detailed cost estimation upfront - Regular budget reviews - Cloud cost optimization - Prioritize features (MVP approach) - Contingency budget (20%)

docs.title: Risk 9: Knowledge Loss
docs.text:
Probability: High Impact: High Description: Loss of mainframe business logic understanding

Mitigation: - Document business rules thoroughly - Involve mainframe experts in migration - Code reviews by business analysts - Comprehensive testing - Knowledge transfer sessions

docs.title: Risk 10: Operational Readiness
docs.text:
Probability: Medium Impact: High Description: Operations team not ready for microservices

Mitigation: - DevOps training - Runbooks and documentation - Monitoring and alerting setup - Incident response procedures - Practice deployments and rollbacks

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Required Software: - Java 17 or 21 (OpenJDK or Oracle JDK) - Maven 3.8+ or Gradle 8+ - Docker Desktop 4.x - PostgreSQL 15+ (or Docker container) - Git - IDE (IntelliJ IDEA, Eclipse, or VS Code) - Postman or similar API testing tool

# Install Java 17 (Ubuntu/Debian)
sudo apt update
sudo apt install openjdk-17-jdk

# Verify installation
java -version

docs.title: 2. Install Maven

# Verify installation

docs.title: 3. Install Docker
docs.text:
# Install Docker (Ubuntu/Debian)
sudo apt install docker.io
sudo systemctl start docker
sudo systemctl enable docker
sudo usermod -aG docker $USER

# Verify installation
docker --version
docker-compose --version

docs.title: 4. Set Up PostgreSQL
docs.text:
Option A: Docker Container (Recommended for Development)

# Create docker-compose.yml for PostgreSQL
cat > docker-compose-postgres.yml << 'EOF'
version: '3.8'
services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:15
    container_name: carddemo-postgres
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: carddemo
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: carddemo123
      POSTGRES_DB: carddemo
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
    volumes:
      - postgres-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    networks:
      - carddemo-network

volumes:
  postgres-data:

networks:
  carddemo-network:
    driver: bridge
EOF

# Start PostgreSQL
docker-compose -f docker-compose-postgres.yml up -d

# Verify PostgreSQL is running
docker ps | grep postgres

Option B: Native Installation

# Install PostgreSQL (Ubuntu/Debian)
sudo apt install postgresql postgresql-contrib

# Start PostgreSQL
sudo systemctl start postgresql
sudo systemctl enable postgresql

# Create database and user
sudo -u postgres psql
CREATE USER carddemo WITH PASSWORD 'carddemo123';
CREATE DATABASE carddemo OWNER carddemo;
GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON DATABASE carddemo TO carddemo;
\q

docs.title: 5. Set Up Redis (Optional)
docs.text:
# Docker container for Redis
docker run -d --name carddemo-redis \
  -p 6379:6379 \
  --network carddemo-network \
  redis:7-alpine

# Verify Redis is running
docker exec -it carddemo-redis redis-cli ping
# Should return: PONG

docs.title: 6. Set Up Kafka (Optional)
docs.text:
# Create docker-compose.yml for Kafka
cat > docker-compose-kafka.yml << 'EOF'
version: '3.8'
services:
  zookeeper:
    image: confluentinc/cp-zookeeper:7.5.0
    environment:
      ZOOKEEPER_CLIENT_PORT: 2181
      ZOOKEEPER_TICK_TIME: 2000
    networks:
      - carddemo-network

  kafka:
    image: confluentinc/cp-kafka:7.5.0
    depends_on:
      - zookeeper
    ports:
      - "9092:9092"
    environment:
      KAFKA_BROKER_ID: 1
      KAFKA_ZOOKEEPER_CONNECT: zookeeper:2181
      KAFKA_ADVERTISED_LISTENERS: PLAINTEXT://localhost:9092
      KAFKA_OFFSETS_TOPIC_REPLICATION_FACTOR: 1
    networks:
      - carddemo-network

networks:
  carddemo-network:
    external: true
EOF

# Start Kafka
docker-compose -f docker-compose-kafka.yml up -d

package com.carddemo.customer.model.entity;

import jakarta.persistence.*;
import lombok.AllArgsConstructor;
import lombok.Builder;
import lombok.Data;
import lombok.NoArgsConstructor;
import org.hibernate.annotations.CreationTimestamp;
import org.hibernate.annotations.UpdateTimestamp;

import java.time.LocalDate;
import java.time.LocalDateTime;

@Entity
@Table(name = "customers", indexes = {
    @Index(name = "idx_customers_ssn", columnList = "ssn"),
    @Index(name = "idx_customers_name", columnList = "last_name, first_name")
})
@Data
@Builder
@NoArgsConstructor
@AllArgsConstructor
public class Customer {

    @Id
    @Column(name = "customer_id", nullable = false)
    private Long customerId;

    @Column(name = "first_name", length = 25, nullable = false)
    private String firstName;

    @Column(name = "middle_name", length = 25)
    private String middleName;

    @Column(name = "last_name", length = 25, nullable = false)
    private String lastName;

    @Column(name = "address_line1", length = 50)
    private String addressLine1;

    @Column(name = "address_line2", length = 50)
    private String addressLine2;

    @Column(name = "address_line3", length = 50)
    private String addressLine3;

    @Column(name = "state_code", length = 2)
    private String stateCode;

    @Column(name = "country_code", length = 3)
    private String countryCode;

    @Column(name = "zip_code", length = 10)
    private String zipCode;

    @Column(name = "phone_number1", length = 15)
    private String phoneNumber1;

    @Column(name = "phone_number2", length = 15)
    private String phoneNumber2;

    @Column(name = "ssn", length = 9)
    private String ssn;

    @Column(name = "govt_issued_id", length = 20)
    private String govtIssuedId;

    @Column(name = "date_of_birth")
    private LocalDate dateOfBirth;

    @Column(name = "eft_account_id", length = 10)
    private String eftAccountId;

    @Column(name = "primary_card_holder_ind", length = 1)
    private String primaryCardHolderInd;

    @Column(name = "fico_credit_score")
    private Short ficoCreditScore;

    @CreationTimestamp
    @Column(name = "created_at", nullable = false, updatable = false)

    @UpdateTimestamp

}

package com.carddemo.customer.repository;

import com.carddemo.customer.model.entity.Customer;
import org.springframework.data.jpa.repository.JpaRepository;
import org.springframework.data.jpa.repository.Query;
import org.springframework.data.repository.query.Param;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Repository;

import java.util.List;
import java.util.Optional;

@Repository
public interface CustomerRepository extends JpaRepository<Customer, Long> {

    Optional<Customer> findBySsn(String ssn);

    List<Customer> findByLastNameContainingIgnoreCase(String lastName);

    @Query("SELECT c FROM Customer c WHERE " +
           "LOWER(c.firstName) LIKE LOWER(CONCAT('%', :searchTerm, '%')) OR " +
           "LOWER(c.lastName) LIKE LOWER(CONCAT('%', :searchTerm, '%'))")
    List<Customer> searchByName(@Param("searchTerm") String searchTerm);

    @Query("SELECT c FROM Customer c WHERE c.stateCode = :stateCode")
    List<Customer> findByState(@Param("stateCode") String stateCode);

    boolean existsBySsn(String ssn);
}

package com.carddemo.customer.service.impl;

import com.carddemo.customer.exception.CustomerNotFoundException;
import com.carddemo.customer.exception.DuplicateCustomerException;
import com.carddemo.customer.model.dto.CustomerRequest;
import com.carddemo.customer.model.dto.CustomerResponse;
import com.carddemo.customer.model.entity.Customer;
import com.carddemo.customer.repository.CustomerRepository;
import com.carddemo.customer.service.CustomerService;
import lombok.RequiredArgsConstructor;
import lombok.extern.slf4j.Slf4j;
import org.springframework.cache.annotation.CacheEvict;
import org.springframework.cache.annotation.Cacheable;
import org.springframework.kafka.core.KafkaTemplate;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import org.springframework.transaction.annotation.Transactional;

import java.util.List;
import java.util.stream.Collectors;

@Service
@RequiredArgsConstructor
@Slf4j
@Transactional
public class CustomerServiceImpl implements CustomerService {

    private final CustomerRepository customerRepository;
    private final KafkaTemplate<String, Object> kafkaTemplate;

    @Override
    public CustomerResponse createCustomer(CustomerRequest request) {
        log.info("Creating customer with SSN: {}", request.getSsn());

        // Check for duplicate SSN
        if (customerRepository.existsBySsn(request.getSsn())) {
            throw new DuplicateCustomerException("Customer with SSN already exists");
        }

        Customer customer = Customer.builder()
            .customerId(request.getCustomerId())
            .firstName(request.getFirstName())
            .middleName(request.getMiddleName())
            .lastName(request.getLastName())
            .addressLine1(request.getAddressLine1())
            .addressLine2(request.getAddressLine2())
            .addressLine3(request.getAddressLine3())
            .stateCode(request.getStateCode())
            .countryCode(request.getCountryCode())
            .zipCode(request.getZipCode())
            .phoneNumber1(request.getPhoneNumber1())
            .phoneNumber2(request.getPhoneNumber2())
            .ssn(request.getSsn())
            .govtIssuedId(request.getGovtIssuedId())
            .dateOfBirth(request.getDateOfBirth())
            .eftAccountId(request.getEftAccountId())
            .primaryCardHolderInd(request.getPrimaryCardHolderInd())
            .ficoCreditScore(request.getFicoCreditScore())
            .build();

        Customer savedCustomer = customerRepository.save(customer);

        // Publish event
        kafkaTemplate.send("customer-events", "customer.created", savedCustomer);

        log.info("Customer created successfully with ID: {}", savedCustomer.getCustomerId());
        return mapToResponse(savedCustomer);
    }

    @Override
    @Cacheable(value = "customers", key = "#customerId")
    @Transactional(readOnly = true)
    public CustomerResponse getCustomer(Long customerId) {
        log.info("Fetching customer with ID: {}", customerId);

        Customer customer = customerRepository.findById(customerId)
            .orElseThrow(() -> new CustomerNotFoundException("Customer not found with ID: " + customerId));

        return mapToResponse(customer);
    }

    @Override
    @CacheEvict(value = "customers", key = "#customerId")
    public CustomerResponse updateCustomer(Long customerId, CustomerRequest request) {
        log.info("Updating customer with ID: {}", customerId);

        Customer customer = customerRepository.findById(customerId)
            .orElseThrow(() -> new CustomerNotFoundException("Customer not found with ID: " + customerId));

        // Update fields
        customer.setFirstName(request.getFirstName());
        customer.setMiddleName(request.getMiddleName());
        customer.setLastName(request.getLastName());
        customer.setAddressLine1(request.getAddressLine1());
        customer.setAddressLine2(request.getAddressLine2());
        customer.setAddressLine3(request.getAddressLine3());
        customer.setStateCode(request.getStateCode());
        customer.setCountryCode(request.getCountryCode());
        customer.setZipCode(request.getZipCode());
        customer.setPhoneNumber1(request.getPhoneNumber1());
        customer.setPhoneNumber2(request.getPhoneNumber2());
        customer.setGovtIssuedId(request.getGovtIssuedId());
        customer.setDateOfBirth(request.getDateOfBirth());
        customer.setEftAccountId(request.getEftAccountId());
        customer.setPrimaryCardHolderInd(request.getPrimaryCardHolderInd());
        customer.setFicoCreditScore(request.getFicoCreditScore());

        Customer updatedCustomer = customerRepository.save(customer);

        // Publish event
        kafkaTemplate.send("customer-events", "customer.updated", updatedCustomer);

        log.info("Customer updated successfully with ID: {}", customerId);
        return mapToResponse(updatedCustomer);
    }

    @Override
    @CacheEvict(value = "customers", key = "#customerId")
    public void deleteCustomer(Long customerId) {
        log.info("Deleting customer with ID: {}", customerId);

        if (!customerRepository.existsById(customerId)) {
            throw new CustomerNotFoundException("Customer not found with ID: " + customerId);
        }

        customerRepository.deleteById(customerId);

        // Publish event
        kafkaTemplate.send("customer-events", "customer.deleted", customerId);

        log.info("Customer deleted successfully with ID: {}", customerId);
    }

    @Override
    @Transactional(readOnly = true)
    public List<CustomerResponse> searchCustomers(String searchTerm) {
        log.info("Searching customers with term: {}", searchTerm);

        List<Customer> customers = customerRepository.searchByName(searchTerm);
        return customers.stream()
            .map(this::mapToResponse)
            .collect(Collectors.toList());
    }

    @Override
    @Transactional(readOnly = true)
    public List<CustomerResponse> getCustomersByState(String stateCode) {
        log.info("Fetching customers for state: {}", stateCode);

        List<Customer> customers = customerRepository.findByState(stateCode);
        return customers.stream()
            .map(this::mapToResponse)
            .collect(Collectors.toList());
    }

    private CustomerResponse mapToResponse(Customer customer) {
        return CustomerResponse.builder()
            .customerId(customer.getCustomerId())
            .firstName(customer.getFirstName())
            .middleName(customer.getMiddleName())
            .lastName(customer.getLastName())
            .addressLine1(customer.getAddressLine1())
            .addressLine2(customer.getAddressLine2())
            .addressLine3(customer.getAddressLine3())
            .stateCode(customer.getStateCode())
            .countryCode(customer.getCountryCode())
            .zipCode(customer.getZipCode())
            .phoneNumber1(customer.getPhoneNumber1())
            .phoneNumber2(customer.getPhoneNumber2())
            .ssn(customer.getSsn())
            .govtIssuedId(customer.getGovtIssuedId())
            .dateOfBirth(customer.getDateOfBirth())
            .eftAccountId(customer.getEftAccountId())
            .primaryCardHolderInd(customer.getPrimaryCardHolderInd())
            .ficoCreditScore(customer.getFicoCreditScore())
            .createdAt(customer.getCreatedAt())
            .updatedAt(customer.getUpdatedAt())
            .build();
    }
}

package com.carddemo.customer.exception;

import lombok.extern.slf4j.Slf4j;
import org.springframework.http.HttpStatus;
import org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity;
import org.springframework.validation.FieldError;
import org.springframework.web.bind.MethodArgumentNotValidException;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.ExceptionHandler;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestControllerAdvice;

import java.time.LocalDateTime;
import java.util.HashMap;
import java.util.Map;

@RestControllerAdvice
@Slf4j
public class GlobalExceptionHandler {

    @ExceptionHandler(CustomerNotFoundException.class)
    public ResponseEntity<ErrorResponse> handleCustomerNotFoundException(CustomerNotFoundException ex) {
        log.error("Customer not found: {}", ex.getMessage());
        ErrorResponse error = ErrorResponse.builder()
            .timestamp(LocalDateTime.now())
            .status(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND.value())
            .error("Not Found")
            .message(ex.getMessage())
            .build();
        return ResponseEntity.status(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND).body(error);
    }

    @ExceptionHandler(DuplicateCustomerException.class)
    public ResponseEntity<ErrorResponse> handleDuplicateCustomerException(DuplicateCustomerException ex) {
        log.error("Duplicate customer: {}", ex.getMessage());
        ErrorResponse error = ErrorResponse.builder()
            .timestamp(LocalDateTime.now())
            .status(HttpStatus.CONFLICT.value())
            .error("Conflict")
            .message(ex.getMessage())
            .build();
        return ResponseEntity.status(HttpStatus.CONFLICT).body(error);
    }

    @ExceptionHandler(MethodArgumentNotValidException.class)
    public ResponseEntity<ErrorResponse> handleValidationExceptions(MethodArgumentNotValidException ex) {
        Map<String, String> errors = new HashMap<>();
        ex.getBindingResult().getAllErrors().forEach((error) -> {
            String fieldName = ((FieldError) error).getField();
            String errorMessage = error.getDefaultMessage();
            errors.put(fieldName, errorMessage);
        });

        ErrorResponse error = ErrorResponse.builder()
            .timestamp(LocalDateTime.now())
            .status(HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST.value())
            .error("Validation Failed")
            .message("Invalid input")
            .validationErrors(errors)
            .build();
        return ResponseEntity.status(HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST).body(error);
    }

    @ExceptionHandler(Exception.class)
    public ResponseEntity<ErrorResponse> handleGenericException(Exception ex) {
        log.error("Unexpected error: {}", ex.getMessage(), ex);
        ErrorResponse error = ErrorResponse.builder()
            .timestamp(LocalDateTime.now())
            .status(HttpStatus.INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR.value())
            .error("Internal Server Error")
            .message("An unexpected error occurred")
            .build();
        return ResponseEntity.status(HttpStatus.INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR).body(error);
    }
}

docs.title: RESTful API Design Principles
docs.text:
1. Resource-Based URLs: Use nouns, not verbs
  2. Good: GET /api/v1/customers/{id}

  3. Bad: GET /api/v1/getCustomer?id={id}

  4. HTTP Methods: Use appropriate HTTP methods

  5. GET: Retrieve resources
  6. POST: Create resources
  7. PUT: Update resources (full update)
  8. PATCH: Partial update

  9. DELETE: Delete resources

  10. Status Codes: Return appropriate HTTP status codes

  11. 200 OK: Successful GET, PUT, PATCH
  12. 201 Created: Successful POST
  13. 204 No Content: Successful DELETE
  14. 400 Bad Request: Invalid input
  15. 401 Unauthorized: Authentication required
  16. 403 Forbidden: Insufficient permissions
  17. 404 Not Found: Resource not found
  18. 409 Conflict: Duplicate resource

  19. 500 Internal Server Error: Server error

  20. Versioning: Use URL versioning

  21. /api/v1/customers

  22. /api/v2/customers

  23. Pagination: Support pagination for list endpoints

  24. /api/v1/customers?page=0&size=20&sort=lastName,asc

  25. Filtering: Support filtering

  26. /api/v1/customers?state=NY&status=ACTIVE

  27. Error Responses: Consistent error format json { "timestamp": "2025-11-21T10:30:00", "status": 404, "error": "Not Found", "message": "Customer not found with ID: 12345", "path": "/api/v1/customers/12345" }

@Service
@RequiredArgsConstructor
@Slf4j
public class DataMigrationService {

    private final JdbcTemplate jdbcTemplate;

    public void importCustomersFromCsv(String csvFilePath) throws IOException {
        log.info("Starting customer data import from: {}", csvFilePath);

        // Disable indexes for faster import
        jdbcTemplate.execute("DROP INDEX IF EXISTS idx_customers_ssn");
        jdbcTemplate.execute("DROP INDEX IF EXISTS idx_customers_name");

        // Use COPY command for bulk import
        String sql = String.format(
            "COPY customers (customer_id, first_name, middle_name, last_name, " +
            "address_line1, address_line2, address_line3, state_code, country_code, " +
            "zip_code, phone_number1, phone_number2, ssn, govt_issued_id, " +
            "date_of_birth, eft_account_id, primary_card_holder_ind, fico_credit_score) " +
            "FROM '%s' DELIMITER ',' CSV HEADER", csvFilePath);

        jdbcTemplate.execute(sql);

        // Recreate indexes
        jdbcTemplate.execute("CREATE INDEX idx_customers_ssn ON customers(ssn)");
        jdbcTemplate.execute("CREATE INDEX idx_customers_name ON customers(last_name, first_name)");

        // Get record count
        Integer count = jdbcTemplate.queryForObject("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customers", Integer.class);
        log.info("Customer data import completed. Records imported: {}", count);
    }

    public void validateMigration() {
        log.info("Validating data migration...");

        // Check record counts
        Integer customerCount = jdbcTemplate.queryForObject(
            "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customers", Integer.class);
        log.info("Customer records: {}", customerCount);

        // Check for null values in required fields
        Integer nullFirstNames = jdbcTemplate.queryForObject(
            "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customers WHERE first_name IS NULL", Integer.class);
        Integer nullLastNames = jdbcTemplate.queryForObject(
            "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customers WHERE last_name IS NULL", Integer.class);

        if (nullFirstNames > 0 || nullLastNames > 0) {
            log.error("Data validation failed: Found null values in required fields");
        } else {
            log.info("Data validation passed");
        }

        // Sample data verification
        List<Customer> samples = jdbcTemplate.query(
            "SELECT * FROM customers LIMIT 10",
            (rs, rowNum) -> mapRowToCustomer(rs));

        samples.forEach(customer -> 
            log.info("Sample customer: {} {} (ID: {})", 
                customer.getFirstName(), customer.getLastName(), customer.getCustomerId()));
    }

    private Customer mapRowToCustomer(ResultSet rs) throws SQLException {
        return Customer.builder()
            .customerId(rs.getLong("customer_id"))
            .firstName(rs.getString("first_name"))
            .lastName(rs.getString("last_name"))
            .build();
    }
}

@ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class)
class CustomerServiceTest {

    @Mock
    private CustomerRepository customerRepository;

    @Mock
    private KafkaTemplate<String, Object> kafkaTemplate;

    @InjectMocks
    private CustomerServiceImpl customerService;

    @Test
    void testCreateCustomer_Success() {
        // Given
        CustomerRequest request = CustomerRequest.builder()
            .customerId(1L)
            .firstName("John")
            .lastName("Doe")
            .ssn("123456789")
            .build();

        Customer customer = Customer.builder()
            .customerId(1L)
            .firstName("John")
            .lastName("Doe")
            .ssn("123456789")
            .build();

        when(customerRepository.existsBySsn(anyString())).thenReturn(false);
        when(customerRepository.save(any(Customer.class))).thenReturn(customer);

        // When
        CustomerResponse response = customerService.createCustomer(request);

        // Then
        assertNotNull(response);
        assertEquals(1L, response.getCustomerId());
        assertEquals("John", response.getFirstName());
        assertEquals("Doe", response.getLastName());

        verify(customerRepository).existsBySsn("123456789");
        verify(customerRepository).save(any(Customer.class));
        verify(kafkaTemplate).send(eq("customer-events"), eq("customer.created"), any());
    }

    @Test
    void testCreateCustomer_DuplicateSSN() {
        // Given
        CustomerRequest request = CustomerRequest.builder()
            .customerId(1L)
            .ssn("123456789")
            .build();

        when(customerRepository.existsBySsn(anyString())).thenReturn(true);

        // When & Then
        assertThrows(DuplicateCustomerException.class, 
            () -> customerService.createCustomer(request));

        verify(customerRepository).existsBySsn("123456789");
        verify(customerRepository, never()).save(any());
    }
}

docs.text:
Test Structure:

@ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class)
class CustomerServiceTest {

    @Mock
    private CustomerRepository customerRepository;

    @Mock
    private KafkaTemplate<String, Object> kafkaTemplate;

    @InjectMocks
    private CustomerServiceImpl customerService;

    @Test
    @DisplayName("Should create customer successfully when valid request provided")
    void testCreateCustomer_Success() {
        // Given (Arrange)
        CustomerRequest request = createValidCustomerRequest();
        Customer expectedCustomer = createCustomerEntity();

        when(customerRepository.existsBySsn(anyString())).thenReturn(false);
        when(customerRepository.save(any(Customer.class))).thenReturn(expectedCustomer);

        // When (Act)
        CustomerResponse response = customerService.createCustomer(request);

        // Then (Assert)
        assertThat(response).isNotNull();
        assertThat(response.getCustomerId()).isEqualTo(1L);
        assertThat(response.getFirstName()).isEqualTo("John");

        verify(customerRepository).existsBySsn("123456789");
        verify(customerRepository).save(any(Customer.class));
        verify(kafkaTemplate).send(eq("customer-events"), eq("customer.created"), any());
    }

    @Test
    @DisplayName("Should throw DuplicateCustomerException when SSN already exists")
    void testCreateCustomer_DuplicateSSN() {
        // Given
        CustomerRequest request = createValidCustomerRequest();
        when(customerRepository.existsBySsn(anyString())).thenReturn(true);

        // When & Then
        assertThatThrownBy(() -> customerService.createCustomer(request))
            .isInstanceOf(DuplicateCustomerException.class)
            .hasMessageContaining("Customer with SSN already exists");

        verify(customerRepository).existsBySsn("123456789");
        verify(customerRepository, never()).save(any());
    }

    private CustomerRequest createValidCustomerRequest() {
        return CustomerRequest.builder()
            .customerId(1L)
            .firstName("John")
            .lastName("Doe")
            .ssn("123456789")
            .build();
    }

    private Customer createCustomerEntity() {
        return Customer.builder()
            .customerId(1L)
            .firstName("John")
            .lastName("Doe")
            .ssn("123456789")
            .build();
    }
}

@SpringBootTest
@EmbeddedKafka(partitions = 1, topics = {"customer-events"})
class CustomerEventIntegrationTest {

    @Autowired
    private KafkaTemplate<String, Object> kafkaTemplate;

    @Autowired
    private CustomerService customerService;

    @Test
    void testCustomerCreatedEventPublished() throws Exception {
        // Given
        CountDownLatch latch = new CountDownLatch(1);
        AtomicReference<CustomerEvent> receivedEvent = new AtomicReference<>();

        // Set up consumer
        @KafkaListener(topics = "customer-events", groupId = "test-group")
        public void listen(ConsumerRecord<String, CustomerEvent> record) {
            receivedEvent.set(record.value());
            latch.countDown();
        }

        CustomerRequest request = createValidCustomerRequest();

        // When
        customerService.createCustomer(request);

        // Then
        assertThat(latch.await(10, TimeUnit.SECONDS)).isTrue();
        assertThat(receivedEvent.get()).isNotNull();
        assertThat(receivedEvent.get().getCustomerId()).isEqualTo(1L);
    }
}
